November 3, 2000
Strawberry: Life Not Worth Living
By VICKIE CHACHERE, Associated Press Writer

TAMPA, Fla. (AP) - Darryl Strawberry told a judge Friday he has lost his will to live. The former baseball star said he has stopped cancer-fighting chemotherapy while in jail and that he left a treatment center for a drug binge he hoped would end his life.
See

Strawberry, 39, speaking in a clear, calm voice, told Circuit Court Judge Florence Foster that the only reason he has not killed himself is that it wouldn't be fair to his five children.

``Life hasn't been worth living for me, that's the honest truth,'' Strawberry said. ``I am not afraid of death.''

The suspended slugger was in court for a hearing on his Oct. 25 arrest for leaving a residential drug treatment center where he was serving a two-year house arrest. Strawberry admitted to using crack cocaine and taking the prescription drug Xanax in the four hours he was gone.

Foster delayed until Nov. 9 deciding whether Strawberry should be sentenced to jail, returned to the drug treatment center or possibly sent to state prison. The judge said she wanted to hear from Strawberry's doctors about the status of his cancer.

Strawberry told the judge that he quit his chemotherapy, which makes him sick for days after a treatment, because it was too much to handle behind bars.

He asked to be released, telling the judge: ``I'm not a danger to society. I've never harmed nobody; I never will.''

" The last couple of weeks of my life have been down hill,'' Strawberry said. ``I basically wanted to die.''

(MarijuanaNews note: Of course, because he is under court control and subject to frequent " drug testing " he will not be able to use medical marijuana. Jeb Bush has made Florida into a bastion of Reefer Madness opposition to medical marijuana.)


See

He said he considered killing himself, but refrained because of his five children.

" So I figured drugs might kill me,'' he said. " Life hasn't been worth living for me. That's the honest truth.''

Defense attorney Joseph Ficarrotta and Timothy Sweeney, the attorney at the treatment center, HealthCare Connections, urged Foster to allow Strawberry to return to the center with the addition of an electronic monitor.

Ficarrotta said Strawberry is being held in an isolation cell in the medical unit for up to 23 hours a day because jail officials believe his celebrity will be disruptive.

HealthCare Connections is a private facility that caters to addicted celebrities, upscale professionals or people who otherwise are well-known in their communities.

" He needs treatment,'' Ficarrotta told the judge. " The court is well aware this man is a very sick individual. This man is worth saving, your honor.''

Prosecutors took a harder line. Assistant State Attorney Steve Wetter said Strawberry likely will just leave the unsecured center again.

The prosecutor had no reaction to Strawberry's talk of ending his life.

``He has shown ... time after time that he can't be trusted,'' Wetter said. ``He's not amenable to treatment. He's in denial.''


(MarijuanaNews note: Who is in denial. Who cannot be trusted?)

Strawberry's state probation officer has recommended that the judge sentence Strawberry to 30 days in jail and then be sent back to the treatment center wearing an electronic monitor that would sound an alarm if Strawberry left again.

The state prison system also has a secured drug treatment center near Tampa that could be considered.

Ronald Dock, Strawberry's friend and mentor through the New York Yankees organization, said jail has shaken Strawberry, but he believes Strawberry is ready to try again to beat his addiction and the disease.

" He's as low as he's ever been,'' said Dock, himself a recovered addict who says he has gone through feelings similar to Strawberry's. Dock said jail has given Strawberry time to think and that he is going through a " spiritual awaking.''

" I knew this would get his attention, if it didn't kill him,'' Dock said. ``Thank God it didn't kill him.''
(MarijuanaNews note: We could say the same thing about marijuana prohibition. If it gets our attention, it won’t kill freedom. Will we really learn from this.?)

Strawberry's house arrest stems from his April 1999 arrest on felony drug charges and allegedly soliciting a prostitute. He was sentenced to house arrest in September if violating his probation while driving under the influence of medication and trying to flee a minor accident.

He faces a court date on those misdemeanor charges later this month.

The 1983 NL Rookie of the Year and eight-time All-Star has had a string of run-ins with the law since the late 1980s. He also has been in and out of drug treatment centers during that time, including the prestigious Betty Ford Center in California.

In February, he was suspended from baseball for a year because of drug use. It was his third drug-related suspension in the five years.

'A big spliff made me feel better'

From The London Daily Telegraph
October 27, 2000
http://www.telegraph.co.uk
See
Two Conservative Papers Endorse Legalization Of Marijuana.

Artist Jonathan Yeo wants to start a proper debate on drugs. Cannabis helped him beat cancer - it could help others, too, he tells Alice Thomson

TOP Tory's son takes drugs. It used to be a great tabloid story, but now half the shadow cabinet has admitted they rolled a spliff in their youth, it seems only dutiful for their children to inhale.

Jonathan Yeo, however, is different. The son of the shadow agriculture secretary is not some young Euan caught roaming around Leicester Square.
(MarijuanaNews note: Euan is a reference to the PM’s son.)
See
Another One We Could Not Make Up: London Police Arrest UK Prime Minister’s 16 Year-Old Son, " Drunk and Incapable'' -- Face Down And Vomiting In Street.

Nor is he like the Tory hierarchy, whose members seem to be determined to show that they are surfing the cultural zeitgeist. The only reason this highly successful portrait artist wants to talk about drugs is that he is convinced they should be legalised.

See
We Are Winning! Measuring the Progress Toward Legalization in the UK – 2 Articles
and links

When he was 22 years old and a film student at Kent University, Jonathan discovered a lump in his neck. The day his father became a Cabinet minister, he found out it was Hodgkin's disease, a malignancy of the lymphoid system. Five years earlier, his 15-year-old sister, Emily, had collapsed at the breakfast table with a brain tumour which paralysed her down one side. The family were told that she had only hours to live, but she is still confounding doctors 12 years on.

" It was extraordinary that our family could be hit twice, " Jonathan says. " But by the time I became ill, my capacity for shock and self-pity had diminished considerably. " Jonathan got through his illness by smoking large quantities of cannabis. As a student, he had taken a medicine cabinet of drugs just for the fun of it. " We tried everything, " he says. But this time it was serious. " I couldn't have got through my fortnightly chemotherapy sessions without smoking dope. The nausea was so overpowering and only cannabis made it better. "

We are sitting in his Knightsbridge studio, with the sun streaming through the windows on to his white canvases. Jonathan is dressed in black except for a pair of silver trainers. He looks so healthy that he should surely be promoting Ashtanga yoga, juicing or rice cakes rather than drugs. " When I got ill, I learnt about the benefits of dope through word of mouth. My doctor said he couldn't condone it but anything that made me feel better was good.
See
80% of UK Doctors " would prescribe cannabis… if they were allowed to. "

Chemotherapy hits your whole system at once. Your body hates it and it makes you feel horribly, revoltingly sick. " See
California Medical Marijuana User With Cancer Prosecuted Despite Letter From Doctor,
" Baseball-Size Lymph Glands "
and
Marijuana Laws Mean Little To The Suffering Says Son Of Cancer Patient

He was given three anti-nausea pills a day, costing £10 each.

See
Costs keeping 'rescue' drugs from patients

" That's a huge bill for the NHS and the pills didn't even do the job, " he says. " Yet a big spliff made me feel better straight away. " Jonathan would come back from the hospital, lie down on the sofa and inhale. " I had some friends who joined me out of sympathy, " he laughs. " It really took the sickness away. I could eat, I could sleep. I stopped worrying. "

After three days, he would feel well enough go to his studio and paint. " I wanted to get some stuff done just in case I didn't live very long. I organised an exhibition and it stopped me becoming negative or depressed. " The day of his last session, the media discovered that his father had been having an affair with a Tory councillor and had an illegitimate daughter. At the same time, he was told that the chemotherapy had only partly worked and he needed radiotherapy. " Everyone thought the family was falling apart, but I wanted to scream, 'we've had far worse than this', " he says.

The side effects of the radiotherapy were different. He felt tired, suffered from terrible headaches and couldn't swallow solid food for several months. " But it was far easier to cope with than the violent nausea. " This is why he feels so strongly that other patients suffering from cancer, MS, ME and other illnesses should be allowed to benefit from smoking cannabis. " It was easy for me to find cannabis. I was a student, all my friends were doing it. The dealers were often other students supplementing their grants. "

He worries about the patients he met at hospital. " When you're very ill, you're told to avoid getting stressed. Yet patients have to go out and find a dealer. They don't know what they're buying or what to do with it. It was worst for the elderly sufferers. "

Jonathan was given a 70 per cent chance of survival. " I sat next to someone who had some rare liver cancer and a five per cent chance of living, " he says. " I felt a complete fraud after that. It's dangerous to generalise, but the people who were getting better were those who were more positive, calm and un-stressed. So dope could really be a life-saver. "

Jonathan is now cured and his portraits are in such demand that he charges £10,000 to £20,000 for them and has a two-year waiting list. He's painted Marco Pierre White, Virginia Bottomley, Archbishop Trevor Huddleston, Matthew Freud, Ross Kemp and a series of extraordinary nudes of his girlfriend, the actress Shebah Ronay. " Portraiture is stigmatised for being old fashioned. I am trying to make it exciting. I want people to try sitting for me who'd never have thought of it before, " he says. He has two ambitions: to paint Tony Blair and to convince him to legalise drugs.

" It's not that I want to take them. I get my kicks out of work. Shebah and I see people who take drugs and they are so boring. Drugs mess up your career and your social life. You should pity those who take them, not criminalise them. " He thinks alcohol can be far more damaging. " It's absurd that Euan Blair gets drunk and everyone says he's just doing normal teenage stuff. Yet if he'd been smoking dope, there would have been an uproar. It's more dangerous lying down in Leicester Square than sitting on a sofa watching television and getting stoned. "

Ann Widdecombe's announcement that the Tories would crack down on anyone caught with a joint between their fingers infuriated him. " William Hague had said he drank 14 pints in one session and she was swigging back Champagne for her birthday. "

And despite the admission by a group of Tory MPs, including his father, that they had tried cannabis when young, Jonathan has no wish to get into party political point-scoring - but he does want a proper debate. " There is always going to be a home secretary or shadow home secretary who wants to pander to the most ill-informed. Drug takers are an easy target. There is no drugs lobby. There is no one to stand up for them or put across the other side of the argument. Politicians get away with saying that soft drugs automatically lead to hard drugs, which is like saying that the caffeine in coffee leads to whisky. "

He cites Holland, where soft drugs have been decriminalised. " The number of people there taking hard drugs has decreased considerably. Only the older generation are doing it. Dutch kids don't want to try the hard stuff because it's less exciting and they don't have to buy their dope off a dealer who also pushes cocaine. "

Jonathan would legalise cannabis first. " Life would get better quite quickly. So many people are affected by violent drunks behaving appallingly. About half the people who get pissed on a Friday night would smoke it to unwind calmly at home. You'll still get people who are dependent on drugs, but then you get drunks sitting on park benches. "

Then, he believes, hard drugs should be legalised. " People are being prescribed hard drugs to keep them off the doctor's hands. A lot are becoming addicted. People take painkillers, uppers, downers, diet pills. I was given so many pills - I had washbags full. You'd think 'these are great' and devour them, your feet wouldn't touch the ground. Then you'd come down with a bump. "

The education, he believes, would be rapid. " We know what cigarettes and alcohol do to us. We know that wine is much weaker than gin and mixing is a disaster. We hardly know anything about drugs. " It all sounds so easy. But isn't he forgetting the people whose lives have been ruined by heroin and cocaine: the addicts, the families, the victims of crime?

" You'd get people becoming dependent, but you'd tax drugs heavily. Heroin and cocaine would be much more expensive, so you'd only do them on your birthday instead of a nice bottle of wine. " Crack, he admits, is more of a problem. " It's highly addictive, but it's also far too cheap. I'd make it £100 instead of £5 a hit. " Gordon Brown would have cocaine-smeared notes piling up in his Treasury. " The responsible thing would be to use it for research and to help former addicts. "

But it would become even easier for children to take drugs. " As a teenager, you go through a phase of wanting to experiment, but at least this way it would be safer. Take ecstasy. Teenagers go clubbing, take a tab and dance for five hours on the trot. It's the most exercise they get all week and it's far healthier than downing a bottle of tequila. There have been a couple of tragic deaths, but I suspect there'd be fewer problems if the stuff was legally made. "

He's also a fan of magic mushrooms. " They are only around for a couple of weeks a year, so you can't go overboard on them. The druids who built Stonehenge knew all about them. They're probably quite healthy compared with fat-laden hamburgers. "

If Jonathan was made the next " drugs tsar " he would start the debate. " The Tories were right to talk about their experiences. Someone said they had their pipe spiked. What sort of moron smokes a pipe at university? The funny thing is, they've done more to put the young off drugs than anything a home secretary could say. A 15 year old listening to nosebleed techno in his bedroom will now rule out dope as embarrassing. "

He is convinced legalising drugs will win votes. " Most people under 50 have tried them. It's ridiculous to turn all those people into criminals. If you make a mistake and go on a binge once or twice it shouldn't ruin your life. In 20 years' time, this will seem like prohibition. "

He now has a perfect life; he doesn't need to go on a drugs crusade. " Getting ill benefited me. It focused me. It was time to stop being an irresponsible kid. There aren't many things worth worrying about in life. Drugs are one of them. "
